chunks: Ahmad ibn Idrees and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Ibn Faddal, from one of our companions, from Sa'd al-Iskaf, who said:

I came to Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام) seeking permission to enter upon him, and there were camel saddles lined up at the door, and the voices had risen. Then a group came out wearing turbans, resembling the Zutt.

He said: So I entered upon Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام) and said: May I be made your ransom, your permission for me was delayed today, and I saw a people come out before me wearing turbans, and I did not recognize them. He said: Do you know who those are, O Sa'd? He said: I said: No. He said: They are your brothers from the jinn. They come to us and ask us about their halal (permissible) and their haram (forbidden), and the features of their religion.

key_terms.أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ: Imam Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام), the one being visited and consulted
key_terms.الْجِنِّ: the jinn, unseen beings who came seeking religious guidance
key_terms.الْعَمَائِمِ: turbans, describing the appearance of the visiting group
key_terms.حَرَامِهِمْ: their forbidden matters according to religious law
key_terms.حَلَالِهِمْ: their permissible matters according to religious law
key_terms.مَعَالِمِ دِينِهِمْ: the teachings and defining features of their religion

ai.seo_question: Did the jinn come to the Imams (عليهم السلام) to ask about halal and haram?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates that a group who appeared unfamiliar to Sa'd al-Iskaf had just visited Imam Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام). The Imam explained that they were brethren from the jinn who came to ask the Imam about their halal, haram, and the teachings of their religion. The report highlights the religious authority of the Imam and the extension of guidance even to the jinn.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Idrees and Muhammad Bn Yahya, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Kufy, from Ibn Fazzal, from one of our comanions, from Sa’d Al Askaf who said,

‘I went over to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> wanting the permission to see him<sup>asws</sup>, so there were riding camels upon the door in a row, and their voices were raised. Then there came out a group turbaned with the turbans resembling the gypsies.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So I went over to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, and I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! Your<sup>asws</sup> permission was delayed upon me today, and I saw a group coming out to me turbaned with the turbans, but I could not recognise them’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And do you know who they are, O Sa’ad?’ I said, ‘No’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They are your brethren from the Jinn. They come to us<sup>asws</sup>, and they ask us about their Permissible and their Prohibitions and the information of their Religion’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ahmad ibn Idris and Muhammad ibn Yahya have narrated from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Kufiy from ibn al-Faddal from certain person of our people from Sa‘d al-Askaf who has said the following.

“Once I to ask permission to meet abu Ja‘far (a.s.). I found saddles of camels lined up in front of the door and noises coming very loud and then a people came out with turbans like those of the Indian gypsies.

I asked abu Ja‘far (a.s.) about them and said, may Allah take my soul in service for your cause. Today it took a long time to receive permission to meet you. I saw a people coming out with turbans whom I could not recognize.” He said, “Do you know, O Sa‘d, who they are?” I said, “No, I do not know.” The Imam (a.s.) said, “They were your brethren in religion from Jinns. They come to us for religious instructions, to learn the lawful and unlawful matters and the principles of their religion.”
